reviews.title: Updated Review 10/6, Please Read
reviews.text:
I really wish Fabulous had a Vacation/Sick Mode or some kind of temporary “Recovery Mode.” 

 I get sick, travel, have procedures, or simply have periods where my daily routines are not realistic (hospitalizations, etc)

Right now, it feels like the app treats these days the same as just skipping or abandoning my habits, when resting while I’m sick is actually part of taking care of myself.

It would be great to have an option to pause my normal routine without losing my progress or feeling like I’ve broken my consistency. A Recovery Mode could even temporarily replace regular habits with things like rest, hydration, medication, easy meals, and sleep, then ease me back into my normal routine when I’m ready.

For an app centered around wellness and sustainable habits, I think this would be an incredibly useful accessibility and self-care feature.

reviews.title: Great Bones, Rough QOL

The prompting, widget shortcut, habits available, and ability to add your own are very nicely done. However, if they simplified the aesthetic and reduced the interruptions users experience while mid-routine trying to check tasks off, the interface would be greatly improved. These are clearly intended to be motivational but have the opposite effect in practice- they’re annoying and make me want to not use the app although it’s helping track habits.

reviews.title: Predatory dark patterns and intentional friction targeting neurodivergent users
reviews.text:
Fabulous markets itself as support for ADHD and habit-building, but its onboarding and subscription model operate on predatory dark patterns designed to trap users in recurring billing.

Here is what is actually happening:

Deceptive Trial Bundling: The onboarding aggressively pushes trial sign-ups across a web of interconnected satellite apps instead of a single, coherent service.

Asymmetric Authentication: You are allowed frictionless one-click Google Sign-In to create accounts and hand over billing details. However, the moment you attempt to cancel, Google Sign-In is disabled, forcing manual credential entry, email verification, and password resets for every individual component.

The Cancellation Maze (Roach Motel): You must navigate multi-step guilt-trips and forced retention surveys for each separate app. Once you finally reach the final cancellation screen for one service, the interface deliberately strips away any "Back" or "Dashboard" navigation. The only visible options are to claim another "free trial," reactivate the subscription, or close the browser tab entirely—forcing you to restart the entire manual login and verification cycle for the next bundled subscription.

Designing exhausting administrative mazes for individuals explicitly seeking help with executive dysfunction and focus is cynical, anti-consumer behavior. Avoid this ecosystem completely. Check your bank statements immediately.

reviews.title: Solid system becoming Interruptive
reviews.text:
I’ve used Fabulous for about 10 years and have genuinely loved it. The Journeys and routines have been one of the most consistent tools in my life for building habits, and I’ve always appreciated how calm and intentional the app felt.

Unfortunately, the newer gamification and frequent pop-ups are starting to interfere with the experience I originally loved. Sometimes I complete one habit in my morning routine and have to dismiss multiple screens about motivation, streaks, daily quests, etc. before I can simply get to my next habit. As a paying user, it’s frustrating—and more importantly, it makes what used to be a very centering morning ritual feel stimulating and irritating.

I really hope Fabulous considers adding a Classic/Focus Mode that allows users to turn off streak prompts, quests, characters, and other gamification while keeping Journeys and routines. I still love the underlying app and would hate to stop using something that has been part of my life for so long because the interface has become too intrusive.

reviews.title: Overwhelming
reviews.text:
I love the actual content and pacing but had to cancel after a single day—the clunky UI, aggressive freemium feature upsells, and multitude of sister apps were too much to handle. I strongly recommend Fabulous workshop the design. As far as the six or so separate apps within the Fabulous family, please reconsider (a) the fragmentation of their product family, and/or (b) provide a gentler ramp to said products. Maybe recommend a single app of the many based on the quiz, and once that’s “settled” by the user, reintroduce the others.

As another reviewer mentioned, there’s an irony that a service intended for an ADHD audience would create such overload and trigger the exact emotional flood, paralysis, and exhaustion chain that are a common struggle for ADHD people—I could feel the aversion settling in.

There are many details I could drill in on, but this covers the broad stokes.

reviews.title: Wait, I can’t choose ZERO STARS? False hope, nasty paywall, and exploitative design. Hy
reviews.text:
I felt like I was given false hope during the questionnaire. All the questions and choices made it feel like I was taking a test about myself! I struggle so badly with lack of motivation, putting things off, and starting a million to-do lists but rarely ever completing just one. While taking the test, the cure for my debilitating lack of drive seemed just a few more questions away. Then I hit the promise-to-pay BS. I don’t even get a chance to see if it works, or see if it’s something I could see myself enjoying enough to stick with. To me, this all feels really, really nasty.

Preying on people who are genuinely struggling just to lock them behind a paywall before they can even try the app is unacceptable. 

But what’s even more unacceptable, bordering on gross is that mobile analytics platforms like Sensor Tower estimate its standalone iOS App Store revenue to bring in roughly $50,000 to $100,000+ MONTHLY, alongside massive legacy backing and funding from major accelerators like Facebook Startup Garage and Microsoft for Startups. 

Critics frequently point out the paradox of a mental wellness app utilizing high-pressure, confusing subscription designs that directly trigger stress in neurodivergent users who struggle with task management (yes!!! and gross!!!). They do not need your money upfront just to show you the basic interface and based on how well the company is purportedly earning every month-they could stand to add a free version with all the paid for features, then create a pro version that gives access to a psychologist, or something along those line. Trust me and avoid this.

reviews.title: This App Fraudulently Charges Subscription Without Even Downloading.
reviews.text:
I received a targeted ad on Facebook over a year ago to do a $1 trial of the program through my web browser. I got a single message sent to the spam email attached to my Facebook account saying I’d be charged $39.99 every other month. It said to activate my premium subscription with a link in that email. I never activated the subscription until today because I didn’t know about it. They never sent a reminder email after clearly knowing the “premium subscription” hadn’t been activated, but they’ll gladly steal money for services not being rendered. How else would you explain me having to click the activation link from 6/14/25 TODAY, make a web account for the first time TODAY, then download the app for the first time ever TODAY to cancel via a web page within the app? I’m disgusted that I was preyed upon for having ADD and my disease process was exploited for their financial gain. It charges Apple Pay, but not in a way that it’d show up under iCloud or App subscriptions. My state law mandates one click cancellation for online only services; this required multiple platforms and excessive clicks through at least 3 minutes worth of this useless program. I have reported this company to the Attorney General and want my $279.93 refunded immediately. Feel free to keep the single $1 I agreed to pay. 

495 other people have mentioned having this problem too, so it’s not my own stupidity. They intentionally conceal their billing and I’m sure the every other month charging helps it from being detected as a recurrent bill/subscription service. This was not picked up by full Norton Financial tracking, nor was it readily identified by other spending trackers. 

These developers should be ashamed of themselves for exploiting folks with mental health conditions. I’ve deleted all social media accounts and have made a dedicated effort to improve my digital hygiene. I’m willingly subscribed to about 10-15 other services, so I do not have an issue with subscription services provided that I’m willingly signing up for them.

reviews.title: The billing practices of this app should be illegal—hundreds of dollars of duplicate bills
reviews.text:
The alarming thing about this app is that it promotes itself as ADHD support then discretely makes multiple frivolous debit card charges that someone with ADHD is less likely to notice happening. Then it creates a tedious hours-long process to correct the matter or unsubscribe from accounts if you want to stop being billed, knowing that many people with ADHD will be too exhausted to go through that. 

wish I could attach a screenshot of my bank statement in which 15 out of the last 20 transactions are duplicate unauthorized charges made by this company long after I canceled my subscription. Even when I signed up they claimed the fee was a monthly charge, but they try to charge me twice a week. 

Here’s what happened. I was signed up for this app for less than 5 minutes before the first duplicate credit card charges started rolling in. The first round was three identical $25 signup charges, which meant they billed me $75, three times what I authorized. I realized my mistake and canceled my account. But—days later, they charged me $75 again in three separate $25 transactions. 

The company simply directs you to their opaque unsubscribe process, saying they won’t stop billing you unless you unsubscribe in the *exact same way* that you signed up. There are several signup methods and they aren’t able to say which one you used. There is no other support that they provide. Unfortunately, unsubscribing is not an option because, according to their systems, I already canceled my subscription. There seem to be multiple ghost accounts I have no access to, there is no way to identify what signup method they think I used so that I could unsubscribe by that process. 

Ultimately, I had to close the bank account they were billing me at, which, again, takes valuable time. But I still get weekly fraud alerts from my bank notifying me this company is still trying to bill the debit card which no longer exists. 

I believe this type of business practice is illegal in my state, and I have reported them, but it needs to be a federal crime.

This app hurt my brain and made me dumber for using it. This app made me financially poorer (even though it’s a free trial). It’s like the D0n@lď Tr¥^^p of apps. Do not—I repeat, do not—take the five star reviews seriously. They simply cannot be real. Have a fine day. 

>>>Fabulous is without doubt the most convoluted & confusing app I think I’ve ever tried using.

Found about this online and took their questionnaire. I agreed to their free trial outside of the app (DO NOT DO THIS!!!) and used Apple’s HideMyEmail feature to protect my anonymity. 

I immediately found myself on a webpage asking for a small fee to pay their people for the “free trial.” I am nice and apparently gullible because I stupidly agreed. Then they sent me to a page that asked me to ¿sign up for other apps? At additional fees? And separate trial periods? Like… I was SOOOO lost! 

So, I downloaded the app and tried signing in… which was a nightmare. It asked me if I wanted to subscribe and stuff despite me providing my email address/username. This got me to thinking that maybe I agreed to one of Fabulous’s sister apps and maybe I didn’t even know what I was trying to do! Then I couldn’t sign into the original website without having to retake the questionnaire again! I finally found a login page which required email verification. I push the button in the email and get directed to the beginning of the questionnaire… AGAIN! 

I honestly have no idea HOW I FINALLY got into the app, but I did. It prompted me to tap on a play icon overlaying a pretty picture of some dude ¿rafting? ¿I think? Which brought me to a list of things me and Fabulous’s little sprites would set out to accomplish. Cute. I pushed on a button… nothing. Couldn’t go back. Couldn’t go forward. I closed the app and HAD TO GO THROUGH THE ENTIRE SIGN IN AGAIN. Did it… bc I’m patient and kind. Landed again on the rafting guy then the list then the nothingness. Redownloaded the app. Same thing. Downloaded one of their sister apps. Couldn’t make heads or tails of it. Finally, in this app, it brought me to a water counting page… because, in order to learn good habits, you must start by counting cups of water… you know…like every other self-help app? 

In the midst of this, my credit card company who could care less about a $1000 out of the blue charge to a kayak company in the middle of the Serengeti called repeatedly until I finally answered asking if I legit made this $10 purchase. That, too, was an absolute nightmare.

I canceled my subscription (I think? Lots of people here say they did too but got hoodwinked and charged later anyway). 

I do not recommend this app. I REALLY do not recommend providing your credit card information to this thing. This app did not help my ADHD and made me feel a certain kind of crazy that I was not aware that I am so capable of.

reviews.title: Subscribe through app store not their app
reviews.text:
Summary, I didn’t find the app helpful after trying twice. For me personally it as annoying. But more importantly, I thought I canceled, apparently didn’t because they don’t make it easy. They charged me for the next year but I had 0 notification & had no idea I had this subscription. I just happened to notice months later. So no notifications about an auto-renewal, no receipt or a cancellation email. They would’ve got away with charging me forever for nothing. 

I have tried this app twice. The first time it was engaging during the trial then no more involved assistance it was basically on you to keep up with your goals. 

Now it’s TOO much going on in the app like a whole story & almost forced you to do things. I only tried for a few days-a month at most & ultimately decided it wasn’t for me. Well last year I guess I didn’t cancel a full 24hrs before the trial ended so they wouldn’t refund my $14 despite having deleted the app & not using it. 

Welp, thank god I don’t use my bank card on Apple pay often because I just noticed in Aug that I was charge yet again for THIS year back in April! Unfortunately I forgot to cancel I guess because they don’t make it easy. I swear I did before deleting the app but you have to do it through their website. But the real issue is that I wasn’t emailed a receipt so had I not stumbled across the payment I would’ve never known & they would’ve kept charging me $14 for nothing every year. Apple sends me a receipt & has all of my subscriptions in one place for review & cancellation. I don’t have to guess or hope I find them. So I highly recommend only subscribing to things through an app store or a credit card that sends you alerts for any payments made. Also turn on notifications for any time any card is charged. Most of mine are on but apparently I didn’t have them on for this bank card. Also my mistake. But still, these companies know what they’re doing. 

Fabulous, you guys need to send receipts & honestly renewal alerts ahead of time for people like myself that weren’t even using the app, to cancel. I also didn’t receive a cancellation email I had to screenshot it for proof. But I immediately received one to come back! That’s shady.

reviews.title: So close…
reviews.text: I really like the app, but it remains very buggy. Where there are places to input text responses, I remain unable to do so. It will just automatically delete each letter I tried to type. Also, it cannot seem to keep up with what day of the week it is. Hope to see some fixes soon.

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text:
I did not simply delete the app and assume that meant my subscription was cancelled. I went into the app, followed the process to cancel my subscription, and received a screen confirming “You have cancelled your subscription.”

And yet… I was charged again.

I contacted support, explained what happened, and requested a refund. They refused.

That’s an unacceptable experience. If your own app tells a customer their subscription has been cancelled, the customer should be able to trust that cancellation.

My advice: don’t trust the cancellation screen. If you cancel, contact support directly, insist on written confirmation by email, and keep an eye on your credit card statements afterward.

I’m leaving this review because I don’t want other customers to learn this lesson the expensive way.

The Fabulous App: 1 star. Would give 0 if I could.

reviews.title: Predatory and dishonest billing
reviews.text: Last week I cancelled my subscription through Apple, which had been charging quarterly for premium. Today I was charged for a full year price. The information available on help.thefabulous.co, where the dev team is directing anyone who had a similar experience, has no clarifying information as to WHY these charges continue after cancellation, only information on how to cancel subscriptions and apply for refunds, leading me to believe that this deception is intentional, which is truly awful for an app that claims to be able mental health. It also gives no further information as to how they continue to access payment info, as this new charge was sent independently without any Apple involvement or record under my subscriptions. If you want to use the app, do not engage in the free trial and do not upload any payment information, but I suggest avoiding it entirely as it also relies heavily on AI in addition to these deceptive billing concerns. I am extremely disappointed as I have recommended this app to others in my capacity as a mental health clinician, will no longer be doing so and will be advising my clients about the predatory billing

reviews.title: Glitches are making me lose motivation
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for years without issue. Then there was an update to add a streak to the daily habits. For whatever reason, if I miss a day, the app doesn’t recognize the calendar day I’m on. Instead, it restarts me on Monday regardless of what day in the week it is. It’s been enough of a frustration and distraction that I’m finding myself not using the app until Monday so the streak days in the app reflect the day I’m living. If I miss a day, I just wait until the following Monday to start over. I’m finding myself using the app less and less, because the streak feature only restarts on Monday. I’ve reached out to the app for support and got nowhere. If this glitch isn’t fixed, I’m not renewing my subscription. The issues in the app are actually sabotaging my motivation and I’ll just find another method to work on my health habits.
